'''Michael Tendler''' ({{langx|ru|Михаил Борисович Тендлер}}; born 1947) is a Swedish Physicist, currently (Emeritus) Professor of [[Nuclear fusion|Fusion]] [[Plasma (physics)|Plasma Physics]] at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]], [[Stockholm]] (KTH). He is the Invited Professor at the Plasma Physics Laboratory Princeton University, USA and the Chubu University, Japan.

== Education ==
He was educated at [[Leningrad State University]] and graduated in Theoretical Physics in 1971 under the supervision of Academician {{Interlanguage link|Vladimir Perel|ru|3=Перель, Владимир Иделевич}}. He left the Soviet Union in 1975 and received his doctorate from [[Uppsala University]] in 1978 under the supervision of Erik T. Karlsson.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.avhandlingar.se/om/Michail+B.+Tendler/ |title=Michail B. Tendler |publisher=Avhandlingar.se |date= |accessdate=2015-10-23}}</ref>

== Career ==
Tendler moved to the Alfven Laboratory of the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) as an associate professor in 1981 and gradually shifted his interest towards Fusion research. From 1992 until 2002 he was an invited professor at the [[Institut national de la recherche scientifique]], [[Université du Québec]], [[Canada]]. He became Full Professor at KTH in 1997. He is the former President of International Congress on Plasma Physics. In 2011 he became the Senior science expert at ITER. Tendler served on the Advisory Committees of National Institute of Fusion Research in [[Toki, Gifu|Toki]] (Japan), the Institute of Plasma Physics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and [[Saint Petersburg State Polytechnic University]].

== Research ==
In the 70s Tendler focused on kinetic and statistical properties of gases and plasmas.<ref>Michail B Tendler 1977 Phys. Scr. 15 59. doi:10.1088/0031-8949/15/1/005</ref> Over time his research shifted towards thermonuclear fusion and has contributed to crucial issues like [[Magnetic confinement fusion|magnetic confinement]] and operation scenarios. In particular he has been instrumental in the theoretical understanding of Plasma rotation and L-H confinement mode transitions.<ref>V. Rozhansky, M. Tendler, “The Effect of the Radial Electric Field on the L-H Transitions in Tokamaks” Physics of Fluids B, Vol. 4, No. 7, 1992</ref>

He elucidated the synergy of neoclassical and turbulence driven flows in a tokamak resulting in improved [[High-confinement mode|H–mode confinement]].<ref>Rozhansky, V. and Tendler, M.: 1996, in: B.B. Kadomitsev (ed.), Reviews of Plasma Physics, Consultants Bureau, New York/London, Vol. 19.</ref> In latter years his research interests broadened into applications of Plasma physics, such as waste treatment  and the implementation of  the DC transmission technology employing High Temperature superconducting cables.<ref>Tendler, M., Rutberg, P., and van Oost, G. 2005. Plasma Based Waste Treatment and Energy Production. Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion 47(5):A219-A230</ref>

Recently, he contributed to novel ideas of enhancing fusion reactions revising the muon catalysis concept.<ref>{{cite conference|first1=Atsuo|last1=Iiyoshi|first2=Yasushi|last2=Kino|first3=Motoyasu|last3=Sato|first4=Yoshiharu|last4=Tanahashi|first5=Norimasa|last5=Yamamoto|first6=Shin|last6=Nakatani|first7=Takuma|last7=Yamashita|first8=Michael|last8=Tendler|first9=Osamu|last9=Motojima|title=Muon catalyzed fusion, present and future|conference=AIP Conference Proceedings 2179, 020010 |year=2019|doi=10.1063/1.5135483|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He  also proposed the new plasma mechanism for the magnetic field generation in the Crab Nebula.<ref name=Crab>{{cite journal|title=On a Possible Mechanism for the Magnetic Field Generation in the Crab Nebula|first1=G.Z.|last1=Machabeli|first2=I.S.|last2=Nanobashvili|first3=M.|last3=Tendler|journal=Physica Scripta|date=1999 |volume=60|number=6|pages=601–605 |doi=10.1238/Physica.Regular.060a00601|bibcode=1999PhyS...60..601M |s2cid=250788833 }}</ref> The mechanism is based upon the development of a two-stream instability resulting from the supernova explosion which took place in 1054 and led to the formation of the Crab Nebula.<ref name=Crab/>

== Awards ==
Tendler was awarded the 1999 [[Ernst Mach Medal]] in Physics by the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.avcr.cz/en/about-us/awards/medals-of-the-cas/the-ernst-mach-honorary-medal-for-merit-in-the-physical-sciences/awarded-medals/|title = Awarded the Ernst Mach Honorary Medals for Merit in the Physical Sciences - Akademie věd České republiky}}</ref>
He was awarded honorary doctorates (Dr.h.c.) from the [[Ghent University]], [[Belgium]], the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], St. Petersburg State Polytechnical University and Chubu University in [[Japan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www3.chubu.ac.jp/main/english/news/27708/|title = Chubu University confers Doctor Honoris Causa to Professor Michael Tendler}}</ref> He is a (foreign) member of the Russian Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-53806.ln-ru|title = Тендлер М.. - Общая информация}}</ref> and the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences.
